why: Which cerebro tools a run holds once its declared tools narrow it (M54.7), as Rust's narrow and its one name test, names_tool (M54.4), decide it: an entry names a tool when, trimmed of the whitespace Rust's str::trim strips and lowercased in ASCII only, it equals the tool's name with or without the mcp__cerebro__ prefix. `allowed_tools` null narrows nothing. `granted` lists what a run the app's TypeScript starts then holds, sorted, and `all` is every such tool: the manifest's base rows that a picker offers. Such a run holds no window, answer or generated proposal tool, and TypeScript cannot read the proposal switch, so none ever appears here; Rust drops them before comparing. The CLI's own tools are not cerebro's and are not listed. Replayed by granted_tools_match_the_shared_cases in src-tauri/src/agent/mod.rs and by src/engine/toolGrant.test.ts, the TS half that decides what a prompt may name.

cases.why: A board create is narrowed through its canvas door.
A canvas edit is narrowed like every other writer.
Notion import is the import writer's scoped note door (M69.5).
Whiteboards narrow through the same scoped read grant (M68.7).
Office document reads narrow through the same grant (M66.8).
Sheet reads and private hypothetical inputs are scoped read tools (M67.2).
Recorded activity is a scoped read tool (M64.2c).
A checked view suggestion is a read-only base tool in the propose picker (M62.4).
Structured database reads narrow through the same names as every other tool (M62.2).
set_fields (M60.4) is a base write row a picker offers, held like any other.
list_notes (M59.5) is a base read row a picker offers, held like any other.
A manifest row that carries the generated prefix by exception (M9.5), held like any other row.
The comment tools (M70.3) are base rows a picker offers, held like any other.
U+0085 and U+3000 are Unicode White_Space, which str::trim strips. JavaScript's trim keeps U+0085.
U+FEFF is not White_Space, so str::trim keeps it and the entry names nothing. JavaScript's trim strips it.
The Kelvin sign lowercases to k in Unicode and not in ASCII, so it names nothing.

cli_why: The CLI's own tools a run holds or may ask for (M57.2), as the tool-approval table plans them (shared/policy/tool-approval.v1.json): `cli` is what its --allowedTools pre-approves and `asks` what an attended run's gate puts to the person. `web` is the web ceiling (M57.7), off where a case leaves it out: on pre-approves WebFetch and WebSearch, and a read limit leaves them alone. An attended run pre-approves its todo list too (M91.1); the subagent tool is left to the CLI, never pre-approved. The narrowing is heard by the same name test as the cases above. Replayed by cli_grants_match_the_shared_cases in src-tauri/src/agent/mod.rs and by src/engine/toolGrant.test.ts, whose cliGrant decides whether a prompt may say the run can change files itself, and whether it may name the web tools.
